title: Passage Two
subtitle: 社交媒体购物与购物成瘾

paragraphs.en: Have you browsed social media late at night, clicked on a brightly colored button and bought something you regretted? Are you hiding parcels from your family? Have you heard of oniomania (购买癖), or shopping addiction?
paragraphs.zh: 你是否曾在深夜浏览社交媒体，点了一个颜色鲜艳的按钮，买下后来让自己后悔的东西？你是否把包裹藏起来，不让家人发现？你听说过“购物癖”（oniomania），也就是购物成瘾吗？

paragraphs.en: Retail is changing. Social media platforms such as TikTok are launching e-commerce features that blur the lines between shopping and entertainment. A whole industry is emerging around livestream shopping, where cheerful hosts turn buying things into a game, by means of quizzes and interactive demonstrations. Regulators and researchers are worried that such innovations are making it harder to resist the urge to spend. Lately a lot of academic papers have been published on shopping addiction.
paragraphs.zh: 零售业正在发生变化。TikTok 等社交媒体平台正在推出电子商务功能，模糊购物与娱乐之间的界限。围绕直播购物，一个完整的行业正在兴起：热情洋溢的主播通过问答游戏和互动演示，把买东西变成一种游戏。监管人员和研究者担忧，这类创新使人们更难抵制消费冲动。最近，已有大量关于购物成瘾的学术论文发表。

paragraphs.en: The problem is not to be taken lightly. Unlike gambling, shopping is something everyone must do, which can make addiction trickier to identify and measure. But academic research covering several countries has suggested that around 5% of people suffer from oniomania. It is more than just the odd impulse purchase; it can ruin people’s relationships and leave them in debt. Avis Cardella, a former shopaholic (购物狂), describes the way she would make purchases as “absent-minded” and “out of control”.
paragraphs.zh: 这一问题不容轻视。与赌博不同，购物是每个人都必须进行的活动，这使购物成瘾更难识别和衡量。不过，覆盖多个国家的学术研究表明，大约 5% 的人患有购物癖。这不仅仅是偶尔的冲动购物；它会破坏人际关系，让人负债累累。曾经是购物狂的阿维斯·卡德拉形容自己过去买东西时“心不在焉”，而且“完全失控”。

paragraphs.en: The features that make shopping easy and fun may also make it more addictive. Shopping has a detectable effect on the brain; it can lead to a surge then a decline in dopamine (多巴胺), a chemical associated with pleasure. “It’s not about the goods,” says Pamela Roberts, a psychotherapist. “It’s the excitement of the spend, the dopamine hit and afterwards the shame.”
paragraphs.zh: 那些让购物变得轻松有趣的功能，也可能使购物更容易令人上瘾。购物会对大脑产生可检测到的影响：它可能使与愉悦感有关的化学物质多巴胺先激增、后下降。“关键不在于买到的商品，”心理治疗师帕梅拉·罗伯茨说，“而在于花钱时的兴奋、多巴胺带来的快感，以及随后出现的羞愧。”

paragraphs.en: Research suggests the sense of community on social platforms, where users share reviews and recommendations, can increase people’s stress and prompt them to spend. A paper published this year in the Journal of Business Research linked irresistible shopping online with a “fear of missing out”, which brands can exploit by showcasing idealised customer experiences or offering time-limited discounts. A paper by researchers in Asia points to “atmospheric cues” in livestreams, such as a host’s entertaining explanations or live chats, that can encourage people to buy.
paragraphs.zh: 研究表明，社交平台上用户分享评价和推荐所形成的社群感，可能增加人们的压力，并促使他们花钱。今年发表在《商业研究杂志》上的一篇论文发现，难以抗拒的网上购物冲动与“错失恐惧”有关。品牌可以展示理想化的顾客体验，或推出限时折扣，利用这种心理。亚洲研究者的另一篇论文则指出，直播中的“氛围线索”——例如主播生动有趣的讲解或实时聊天——也会鼓励人们购买商品。

paragraphs.en: However, any regulatory efforts to reintroduce resistance into the shopping experience may be unpopular with consumers. And technological tricks won’t make addicts of everyone. As Mark Griffiths, an addiction expert at Nottingham Trent University, puts it: “There is a fine line between exploitation and enhancement.”
paragraphs.zh: 然而，任何试图重新为购物过程设置阻力的监管措施，都可能不受消费者欢迎。而技术上的种种手段也不会让每个人都成瘾。正如诺丁汉特伦特大学的成瘾问题专家马克·格里菲思所说：“利用消费者与改善消费体验之间，只有一线之隔。”

questions.en: What do we learn about oniomania from the first paragraph?
questions.zh: 从第一段中，我们了解到关于购物癖的什么信息？

options.en: It is a kind of gambling addiction that is hard to get rid of.
options.zh: 它是一种难以戒除的赌博成瘾。

options.en: It refers to the addiction to shopping that makes people regretful.
options.zh: 它指让人买完东西后感到后悔的购物成瘾。

options.en: It is a rare mental problem that only occurs in large extended families.
options.zh: 它是一种只发生在大家庭中的罕见精神问题。

options.en: It only happens when people shop in social media platforms.
options.zh: 它只会在人们通过社交媒体平台购物时发生。

questions.explanation: 第一段以深夜冲动购物后后悔、向家人藏包裹等行为引出 oniomania，并明确说明它就是 shopping addiction（购物成瘾）。因此 B 最符合文意。
questions.evidence: …bought something you regretted? Are you hiding parcels from your family? Have you heard of oniomania (购买癖), or shopping addiction?

questions.en: Why are regulators and researchers concerned about new retail forms?
questions.zh: 为什么监管者和研究人员担忧新型零售形式？

options.en: Because these forms make shopping more entertaining.
options.zh: 因为这些形式让购物更有娱乐性。

options.en: Because these forms provide interactive demonstrations frequently.
options.zh: 因为这些形式经常提供互动展示。

options.en: Because these forms reduce people’s desire to buy goods.
options.zh: 因为这些形式降低了人们购买商品的欲望。

options.en: Because these forms make it harder for people to control impulsive spending.
options.zh: 因为这些形式让人们更难控制冲动消费。

questions.explanation: 第二段说，娱乐化、游戏化的购物创新让人们更难抵制花钱的冲动，D 正好概括了担忧的核心；A、B 只是形式上的特点，C 与原文相反。
questions.evidence: Regulators and researchers are worried that such innovations are making it harder to resist the urge to spend.

questions.en: What makes shopping addiction more difficult to identify than gambling addiction?
questions.zh: 为什么购物成瘾比赌博成瘾更难识别？

options.en: Shopping involves smaller amounts of money.
options.zh: 购物涉及的金额较少。

options.en: Shopping is a necessary activity for everyone.
options.zh: 购物是每个人都必须进行的活动。

options.en: Gambling addiction has clearer physical symptoms.
options.zh: 赌博成瘾有更明显的身体症状。

options.en: Fewer people admit to having a shopping addiction.
options.zh: 更少的人承认自己有购物成瘾问题。

questions.explanation: 第三段明确指出“与赌博不同，购物是人人都必须做的事情”，因而更难界定哪些购物行为属于成瘾。
questions.evidence: Unlike gambling, shopping is something everyone must do, which can make addiction trickier to identify and measure.

questions.en: What is Pamela Roberts’ explanation for shopping addiction?
questions.zh: 帕梅拉·罗伯茨如何解释购物成瘾？

options.en: It is mainly about acquiring high-quality goods.
options.zh: 它主要是为了获得高质量的商品。

options.en: It satisfies people’s deep need for the idealised customer image.
options.zh: 它满足人们对理想化消费者形象的深层需求。

options.en: It provides a short-term pleasure followed by negative feelings.
options.zh: 它带来短暂的快感，随后出现负面情绪。

options.en: It helps people temporarily escape from real-life financial pressures.
options.zh: 它帮助人们暂时逃避现实中的经济压力。

questions.explanation: 第四段说明购物会引发多巴胺先升后降，罗伯茨特别强调“花钱时兴奋—多巴胺快感—之后羞愧”的过程，与 C 的“先愉悦、后负面感受”一致。
questions.evidence: “It’s the excitement of the spend, the dopamine hit and afterwards the shame.”

questions.en: What factor may push people to spend more on social platforms?
questions.zh: 什么因素可能促使人们在社交平台上花更多钱？

options.en: The sense of community that brings pressure on users.
options.zh: 给用户带来压力的社群归属感。

options.en: The lack of product reviews and recommendations on platforms.
options.zh: 平台上缺少商品评价和推荐。

options.en: The long-term discounts provided by famous brands.
options.zh: 知名品牌提供的长期折扣。

options.en: The boring atmosphere during the live-stream shopping process.
options.zh: 直播购物过程中乏味的气氛。

questions.explanation: 第五段开头直接指出，社交平台上的社群感会增加人们的压力并促使其消费，因此选 A。B 与“分享评论和推荐”相反；C 应是“限时折扣”；D 与主播营造的热闹氛围相反。
questions.evidence: The sense of community on social platforms, where users share reviews and recommendations, can increase people’s stress and prompt them to spend.
